_note: Common hurt points for each condition, from clinical guidance and lived-experience accounts. General guidance only: always defer to the person's own triggers. Pending clinician review.

items.why: It can land as 'your feelings are the problem', which feeds the fear of being too much to love.
items.instead: this is a lot for me to take in, give me a second

items.phrase: "I need space" with no time to come back
items.why: Without a time to come back, a pause can feel like being left.
items.instead: I need a little time to think, and I'll come back to you in an hour

items.pattern: \b(i'?m done|we'?re done|i can'?t do this anymore|maybe we should break up)\b
items.phrase: "I'm done" or "I can't do this anymore"
items.why: It sounds like the relationship is ending, which can set off panic about being abandoned.
items.instead: I'm overwhelmed and need to pause, not leave

items.why: Labels like these cut straight to shame.

items.pattern: \b(just )?(think|be) positive\b|\bcheer up\b|\blook on the bright side\b
items.why: It suggests the low mood is a choice, which adds guilt on top of it.
items.instead: I'm here with you, even on the heavy days

items.pattern: \bsnap out of it\b|\bget over it\b|\bmove on already\b
items.phrase: "snap out of it" or "get over it"
items.why: Depression can't be switched off, so this can make someone feel like they're failing.

items.pattern: \b(others|other people|people) have it worse\b|\bit could be worse\b
items.why: Comparing pain makes people feel they're not allowed to struggle.
items.instead: what you're going through is real

items.why: Low energy is part of depression. 'Lazy' turns a symptom into a character flaw.
items.instead: I've noticed it's been hard to get going lately

items.why: It dismisses something that is very real to them.
items.instead: I believe you that this is hard

items.why: An open-ended message leaves an anxious mind to fill in the worst case.
items.instead: can we talk later? Nothing scary, I just want us to sort something out

items.why: Being told not to worry doesn't stop the worry, and can feel dismissive.
items.instead: I get why that's worrying you

items.why: It can feel like the anxiety is being mocked instead of understood.
items.instead: I can see this is weighing on you

items.why: It leaves an open loop that anxiety keeps circling back to.
items.instead: it's something small, I'll explain properly in a bit

items.why: Weight and eating can be a painful, hard-to-control part of PCOS, so these land as shame.
Skin and hair changes can be a sore spot with PCOS.

items.phrase: remarks about fertility or having kids
items.why: Fertility can be a deep worry with PCOS.

items.pattern: \bit'?s (just )?(your )?hormones\b|\bis it that time\b|\bare you on your period\b
items.why: Writing feelings off as 'just hormones' feels dismissive.
